problem.text: The parser required --mode even when --modes requested only a listing, preventing discovery without supplying a placeholder mode.

reasoning.text: The two control-flow edits work together: defaulting mode to None lets parsing succeed, and treating None as a listing request prevents the subsequent prompt_formats lookup from receiving that sentinel.

impact.text: Listing returns before template construction and model loading. The shared parser still requires -m/--model_dir, although the listing path does not open that directory.

source_notes.text: The root usage-evaluation entry was read; it establishes the existing manually selected chat templates and their BOS/stop policies, rather than automatic checkpoint-template detection.

Issue #12 is titled “Qwen2.5 Coder 0.5B Instruct | ValueError: Unsupported type in stop_conditions.” Its initial problem involved using llama3 mode for Qwen; a later comment separately complains that listing requires a mode, and turboderp promises a fix. Its relationship to this change is inferred from that exact CLI complaint, not an explicit commit reference.

Other inspected discussions concern different problems: #6, “No ROCm runtime is found, using ROCM_HOME='/usr',” reports an import/build failure; #39, “Gemma 3 architecture not in list?”, concerns architecture availability and later frontend behavior; #43, “Error converting abliterated Qwen3 mlabonne/Qwen3-30B-A3B-abliterated,” concerns invalid conversion states; PR #22, “OpenAI compatible API example,” proposes an API frontend. Their chat.py references do not establish that this CLI change fixes those problems.

limitations: The execution check transcribed only the relevant argparse declarations and branch predicate; it did not import or execute chat.py, load a model, or test GPU inference.
Listing still follows module-level imports, so this change does not provide dependency-free discovery.
The Phi4 description is advisory; checkpoint-specific template compatibility was not independently verified.

chapters.title: Discovering chat modes without selecting one

claims.text: Omitting --mode now lists registered modes and returns, even without --modes. Explicit --modes retains priority over any supplied mode. A supplied mode without --modes still follows the unchanged dictionary lookup; the change does not add mode validation or automatic selection.

A bounded standard-library parser transcription confirmed that providing -m unused with either --modes or no mode changes from parser exit 2 to listing. --modes alone still exits 2 because -m remains required. An arbitrary supplied mode plus --modes already reached listing before this change.

The listing reads class descriptions directly from prompt_formats. Updating the Phi description therefore exposes the warning that some Phi4 models use ChatML without changing either formatter: phi retains its system/user/assistant markers and BOS insertion, while chatml retains im_start/im_end markers and disables added BOS.

annotation.summary: Makes chat mode selection optional for discovery and adds a Phi4/ChatML advisory; a model-directory argument remains required.
